whatContradictedTheCard: None on the core design -- the fix landed exactly as scoped. Two process frictions surfaced and were resolved without deviating from the dispatch: (1) the initial worktree path/branch I created (P:/tmp/hauska-factory-build-tags, feat/parcel-build-tags, both matching the queue claim's own naming) diverged from what the planner had actually pre-registered in the seat registry (P:/tmp/hauska-factory-buildtags, feat/build-tags) -- the seat-worktree-gate hook refused twice and both refusals were honored by renaming rather than bypassing, per this session's standing discipline; (2) baking $BUILD_ID directly into the _IMAGE_TAG substitution's own default (rather than appending it at each use site) was considered and rejected before implementing, since Cloud Build substitution defaults are not re-scanned for built-in expansion -- verified this understanding before committing to the simpler, certain-to-work use-site-suffix approach rather than discovering the failure after a submitted build.
constraintsHonored: did not restructure any build file's step order, count, or job-deploy arguments
kept the fix simple and mechanical: one substitution suffix pattern, applied identically across all five files
verified the digest-shape regex against a real, live gcloud artifacts docker images describe output before trusting it, rather than guessing the format
verify-by-violation run for real against production Cloud Build/Artifact Registry, not simulated or asserted
seat-worktree-gate refusals honored by correcting the path/branch to match the registry, never bypassed

LESSON: Cloud Build substitution defaults (the substitutions: block) are literal strings, not re-scanned for built-in variable expansion -- a built-in like $BUILD_ID must be referenced directly at each use site in steps/images, not baked into a user substitution's own default value. Verified before implementing, not discovered after a failed submission.

gcloud artifacts docker images describe --format='value(image_summary.fully_qualified_digest)' returns the FULL form IMAGE_PATH@sha256:HASH, not a bare sha256:HASH -- confirmed live before writing a shape-validating regex against it, since a wrong assumption here would have broken every future deploy job silently.

A queue claim's own --branch/--worktree flags are not authoritative over what the planner has separately pre-registered in _catalog/seat_register.json for the same card -- check the registry directly (or let the gate's refusal message state the exact expected path/branch) rather than trusting the claim command's own naming.
